reasons: No automated test or check was found for this data file.
Several ids and origin values must match other files by hand, and nothing checks them.

terms.meaning: A file that holds information for the app to show, rather than instructions for what to do.
A named description of the fields a piece of data must have, so every entry has the same shape.
A short name made of lowercase words and dashes, used in web addresses and as a stable id.
Where a build came from: a company role or independently.

sections.name: Build
sections.title: Shape of a build entry
sections.what: Defines what every build must include: an id, a name, a status, a type of tool or platform, tags, plain and technical descriptions, a one-line tagline, and optional process text, code link, live link and origin.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed shape keeps every build complete and consistent for the pages that show them.
sections.watch_out: The status is fixed to a single value, LIVE, so a build that is not yet live cannot be added without changing this shape.

sections.name: builds (part 1)
sections.title: Financial, solar cost and scheduling builds
sections.what: Describes the first builds: Abacus, a multi-agent financial modelling tool; Groundwork, an interactive solar cost model; and the start of the Digital Twin scheduling tool. Each has plain and technical text, a process write-up, and a code link, except that the Digital Twin entry is continued in the next section.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the order of the list.
sections.watch_out: The process write-ups describe how each tool works in detail, so they must be edited by hand whenever the tool changes.

sections.name: builds (part 2)
sections.title: Scheduling, portfolio and document build details
sections.what: Continues the Digital Twin architecture, which has a scheduling front end and back end, then describes the Watchtower portfolio monitor and the start of Needle, the document search tool.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The write-ups explain how each tool works for a reader.
sections.watch_out: The Digital Twin entry has no code link, so readers cannot reach its source from this entry.

sections.name: builds (part 3)
sections.title: Document search, planning and platform builds
sections.what: Finishes the Needle document search write-up, describes the Blueprint planning tool (a chain of four agents that check each other), and starts the Haus Nous strategy platform write-up.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Blueprint has no code link, so the only public record of how it works is this text.

sections.name: builds (part 4)
sections.title: Haus Nous, Pulse, Yardstick and First Draft
sections.what: Finishes the Haus Nous write-up, then describes the Pulse survey pipeline, the Yardstick benchmarking tool, the First Draft proposal generator, and the start of the Maate family health app.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Yardstick has a very short description and no process write-up, so it is much thinner than the other entries.

sections.name: builds (part 5)
sections.title: Maate, Hitman, Career OS and Bhoomi Setu
sections.what: Describes Maate, a preventive elder care app, Hitman, a cricket prediction platform, Career OS, a career simulator, and the start of Bhoomi Setu, a land records tool with a multi-step evidence process. These are independent builds, not made in a company role. Parts of the Bhoomi Setu technical text were cut off in the view used for these notes.
sections.why: Likely reason: these were made independently, so they are marked with an origin of independent instead of a company role.
sections.watch_out: Some descriptions make firm claims, such as Hitman scoring on skill alone, and the code here does not verify them.

sections.name: builds (part 6)
sections.title: Bhoomi Setu, Momentum OS, PIT and Cartograph
sections.what: Finishes the Bhoomi Setu write-up, then describes Momentum OS, a personal productivity system, the Project Intelligence Toolkit, a research workspace for capital projects, and Cartograph, a tool that estimates the value of process changes and lists its design principles. The technical text of Cartograph was cut off in the view used for these notes, so only its main ideas are described here.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Cartograph has no code link and no live link, so readers can learn its design only through this text.

summary: Holds the full list of the owner's builds, which are tools and platforms, with names, tags, plain and technical descriptions, and links to code or live demos.
purpose: Serves as the single source for builds shown on the site and lets other data files link skills, roles and curiosities to them.
why: Likely reason: all builds live in one list so the site pages and the connected data stay consistent. No other reason is stated in the code.
how: First, a build's shape is defined. Then each build is listed in order with an origin, which is the role that made it or independent. Each build has a plain description, a technical description, and an optional long process write-up. Code and live links are optional.
inputs: Typed in by hand. The file reads no outside data.
outputs: An exported list of builds that other files read and search by id.
risks: Links are typed by hand and can go stale. Nothing checks that ids are unique or that origin values match a real role. The long write-ups must be edited by hand when a tool changes.
debug: If a build does not appear, check that its entry is in the list and that its id matches the entry in projects.ts. If a link is missing, check the code or live field and the origin value. If text looks wrong, find the matching template text in that entry.
